A1.justification: Both complete 19-page PDFs describe the same FreeMCG work and include Appendices A–G. Full-text comparison and rendering establish that the substantive text, equations, tables, and figures match.

before.justification: v1 reports original counterfactual-generation and feature-attribution experiments on ImageNet and MIMIC-CXR, including quantitative results, qualitative examples, and human-study outcomes.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including Tables 1–2, Figure 5, and the supplementary experiments.

M1.justification: The FreeMCG estimator, diffusion-based particle generation, and feature-attribution and counterfactual procedures in Section 3 and Algorithms 1–3 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use ImageNet and MIMIC-CXR for counterfactual generation and feature attribution, retaining the same lesion classes, counterfactual directions, and illustrated scenarios.

E2.justification: Counterfactual comparisons retain DVCE and LDCE on ImageNet and DVCE on CXR. Attribution comparisons retain Gradient, Integrated Gradients, InputXGradient, and SHAP.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendices E–G retain the same image resolution, 1,000 ImageNet counterfactuals, WordNet target selection, ROAD metrics, model configurations, sampling settings, and five-point human ratings.

E4.justification: The CXR case studies, classifier-architecture comparisons, latent-diffusion examples, and channel-count observations in Appendices B–F are unchanged. No ablation, robustness test, or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Statistical and uncertainty reporting is identical, including Tables 1–2 and Figure 5. No repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-reporting information is added or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results match. For example, Table 1 retains FreeMCG's flip rate of 51.5 and perceived-change score of 3.74, while Table 2 retains its CXR flip rate of 99.2. Figure 5 and appendix examples are also unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, gradient derivations, assumptions, Theorems 1–2, and their Appendix A proofs are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about unified black-box XAI, manifold-constrained gradient estimation, and state-of-the-art counterfactual and attribution performance.

C2.justification: Interpretations of meaningful changes versus flip rate, attribution faithfulness, CXR spurious correlations, and text-conditioning bias are unchanged. Qualifications about hyperparameter sensitivity and computational cost also remain identical.

D1.justification: Appendices E–G retain identical implementation details, including 100 particles per timestep, timestep choices, sampling iterations, model descriptions, source URLs, and user-study instructions.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and all 55 references are unchanged, as is the positioning relative to gradient-based XAI, diffusion counterfactual methods, and ensemble Kalman methods.

P1.justification: The sole visible textual edit is the first-page arXiv margin stamp, changing from v1 dated 22 Nov 2024 to v2 dated 21 Jul 2025. The paper's wording, headings, and section organization are otherwise identical.

P2.justification: Figures, tables, captions, and page layouts are unchanged. Pages 2–19 render identically; page 1 differs only in the version/date stamp.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, empirical evidence, proofs, reproducibility details, and presentation are unchanged throughout the main paper and appendices. Updating the arXiv version/date stamp produces no meaningful gain or loss in overall paper quality.
